text:
sai: Heads-up — we're seeing sustained inter-zone egress latency spikes from eu-west -> eu-central since ~02:30 UTC. p95 token latency up ~220ms (baseline ~40ms). looks correlated with a few large embeddings tenants sitting in the shadowpool. anyone else seeing this?

elaine: Saw alerts and a couple user reports. Grafana panel: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress/egress-latency?var-region=eu-west. ops-bot created incident #5402. :warning:

rob: Can confirm spikes at the proxy level. TCP retrans stats don't show link flaps. quick check: `kubectl -n infra exec -it probe -- curl -sS "http://egress-metrics:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(tcp_retransmissions[1m])"` returned normal ranges.

maria: On the tenant side, org-247 and org-652 are doing huge embedding runs to eu-central storage. Both are on shared slices in the shadowpool and warmed KV cache aggressively this morning — I think kvcache churn + burst egress is the culprit.

sai: Proposed plan: 1) soft-quarantine org-247 for 15m to validate latency improvement; 2) route heavy egress allocs from shadowpool to dedicated-ephemeral slices as a fallback; 3) enable KV-cache-bypass for those organs to reduce churn. Cost tradeoff: estimated +$0.6k/day if we run dedicated burst capacity.

elaine: +1 on soft-quarantine. How do we flip routing quickly? allocator flag or runtime policy?

rob: I can toggle an allocator flag on a canary rack. Example call: `curl -XPOST http://allocator-api/flags -d '{"flag":"shadowpool-prefer-dedicated","value":true,"scope":"rack:eu-w-12"}'` — that'll bias new allocs into ephemeral dedicated slices for that rack group.

maria: Also suggest enabling prefix-KV cache bypass for embedding requests to avoid the regen churn — small config change on the routing proxy.

sai: Rob, please flip the canary and I'll create the short runbook for the soft-quarantine.

ops-bot: deploybot: flag toggled by rob at 1714209930. incident #5402 updated.

rob: Flag is ON for eu-w-12. Initial telemetry: p95 for inter-zone down to ~110ms in that rack (from 220ms).

elaine: That's promising. Can you measure cross-rack impact (does it push load elsewhere)?

rob: Cross-rack p95 improved too — eu-w aggregate p95 from 120ms -> ~90ms after migration started. No obvious spillover to other regions yet.

maria: Quarantine traffic shows org-247 egress reduced by ~75%. org-652 remains heavy; likely needs a planned migration.

sai: Next steps: schedule org-652 migration to dedicated-ephemeral (solutions to notify customer), enable KV bypass for both tenants, and enable cost-metering. Estimated incremental egress cost ~+$0.4k/day for org-652.

elaine: I'll ping oncall for SLA exemptions and make sure we capture the cost approval.

ops-bot: oncall paged: @oncall-eng <oncall@redwood.com>.

rob: If no regressions in 10m I'll roll the allocator bias across eu-west racks.

sai: Thanks — we'll reconvene in 30m and post a short summary to #incidents if stable. :thumbsup:
